**First Studio Ghibli winner – “Spirited Away”** | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | **Film** | *Spirited Away* (宮崎駿 / Hayao Miyazaki) | | **Release Date** | March 20, 2001 (Japan) | | **Award** | **Picture of the Year** – 25th Japan Academy Film Prize (held February 23, 2002) | > *“Spirited Away” became the very first feature‑length work created by Studio Ghibli to capture the top honor of the Japan Academy Film Prize.* > Prior to 2002, the academy’s Picture‑of‑the‑Year winners were almost exclusively live‑action dramas; the only previous Ghibli entry that received major recognition was *Grave of the Fireflies*, which earned the “Best Animation” trophy in 1989 but not the overall title. --- ### How its box‑office triumph amplified Ghibli’s global standing | Domestic Impact | International Ripple Effect | |-----------------|-----------------------------| | • Grossed **¥12.5 billion (~US$120 million)** in Japan – the highest‑grossing Japanese film of 2001.
• Became the most successful theatrical release ever in Japan up to that point. | • Earned **≈US$350 million worldwide**, topping the list of foreign‑language blockbusters in several markets (USA, UK, France, Germany, South Korea).
• Sparked a surge in demand for subtitled/dubbed versions, prompting distributors to license more Ghibli titles for Western audiences. | | • Generated extensive media coverage (“The movie that made everyone talk”), turning the film into a national phenomenon. | • Attracted attention from Hollywood studios; Disney secured exclusive U.S. distribution rights for *Spirited Away* and subsequently acquired a long‑term partnership with Ghibli for worldwide releases. | | • Created a new benchmark for animated cinema in Japan, encouraging higher budgets and ambitious storytelling within the industry. | • Inspired a wave of independent animators and production companies worldwide who cited *Spirited Away* as a creative catalyst. | | • Established a template for cross‑media merchandising (toys, apparel, theme park attractions), reinforcing brand loyalty among fans. | • Led to the creation of dedicated fan communities online, forums, and conventions celebrating Ghibli lore, further expanding the franchise’s reach beyond traditional cinemas. | #### Bottom line Because *Spirited Away* dominated both the domestic market and the international box office while clinching the coveted Picture‑of‑the‑Year award, it served as a launchpad that elevated Studio Ghibli from a respected niche studio to a household name worldwide. The financial proof‑point convinced distributors, broadcasters, and streaming platforms that Ghibli content could command premium prices and wide audience appeal—a reality that continues to shape the studio’s strategy today.
